content_sections.heading: Punjab and Haryana High Court Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: Both the Driver and Frash recruitment notices share the same application timeline. The High Court has stated that the cut-off date to apply is sacrosanct and no application will be accepted after the closing date.

content_sections.heading: Punjab and Haryana High Court Driver and Frash Vacancy 2026: Category-wise Details
content_sections.text: Together, the two notices cover 56 posts. The High Court has clarified that the number of vacancies may increase or decrease depending on the number of vacancies as on the date of preparation of the merit list, for both posts.

content_sections.heading: Punjab and Haryana High Court Driver and Frash Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Candidates in all categories, for both posts, must not be less than 18 years and not more than 35 years of age as on 18/09/2026. For Ex-servicemen, the upper age limit is relaxed by the number of years equal to their defence service plus 3 years. Candidates should ensure that they meet the prescribed age limit as on the specified cut-off date. You can use our Age Calculator to check your exact age and confirm your eligibility before applying. The candidate should be at least 10+2 pass with Punjabi/Hindi as one of the subjects in the matriculation examination. The candidate should possess a valid Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) driving licence. No presumption of eligibility to drive an LMV will be drawn merely on the basis of any higher category endorsed on the driving licence. The candidate should not have been convicted of any offence for negligent driving and must have a minimum of two years' experience of driving a car. Knowledge of Hindi and the regional language. No further formal educational qualification is specified in the notification. Proof of date of birth is admissible only through the Matriculation Certificate (for matriculate or higher candidates) or the Birth Certificate issued by the Registrar of Births and Deaths (for candidates with qualification less than Matric).

content_sections.heading: Punjab and Haryana High Court Driver and Frash Application Fee
content_sections.text: The application fee for both posts is payable online and is non-refundable, with online transaction charges levied extra. For the Frash post only, there is no application fee for candidates who are dependents of Ex-servicemen disabled or deceased during active operation, provided they upload the requisite proof at the time of application and produce the original at testimonials checking. For both posts, reservation and fee relaxation for SC/ST/BC candidates apply only to those holding a valid certificate and domiciled/permanent resident of Punjab, Haryana, or U.T. Chandigarh; candidates from other states are considered under the General Category. Ex-servicemen fee relaxation applies only to the ex-servicemen themselves, not their dependents.

content_sections.heading: Punjab and Haryana High Court Driver and Frash Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection to the post of Driver is made on the basis of performance in a Practical Test-cum-Interview. The High Court may apply any suitable shortlisting criteria for provisionally allowing candidates to appear, informed via a public notice at the appropriate time. Selection does not confer any right to claim appointment; candidates proposed for appointment first undergo a trial period, with confirmed appointment only after its successful completion. Candidates for the post of Frash are selected on the basis of performance in an Interview of 50 marks (25 marks for Suitability to the Job, 25 marks for Etiquette/Manners). Candidates equivalent to 4 times (category-wise) the advertised vacancies, in order of merit in the interview, are then called for a qualifying Physical Endurance Test (PET): an 800-metre race, long jump, and high jump. Failing any one event disqualifies a candidate from the next event. The final list of provisionally selected Frash candidates, as per the number of vacancies advertised across all categories, is prepared from those who qualify the PET, strictly on the basis of their merit in the interview.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for Punjab and Haryana High Court Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: The link for submission of the online application form for both posts is available only on the official website of the High Court, www.highcourtchd.gov.in. Applications for both notices must be submitted online between 28/08/2026 and 18/09/2026. Candidates must apply separately for each post they wish to be considered for. Visit the official website www.highcourtchd.gov.in. Locate the online application link for Employment Notice No. 04/DRV/HC/2026 (Driver) or 05/Frash/HC/2026 (Frash), as applicable. Register with a valid, active personal e-mail ID and mobile number. Fill in personal details and category correctly; no changes are permitted after submission. Upload a recent scanned passport-size photograph (not more than 30 days old, white background) and scanned signature. Pay the applicable application fee online through the available payment options (or upload proof of fee exemption, where applicable for Frash). Review all entries carefully before final submission, and retain a printed copy of the submitted application form. Proof of qualification and date of birth (Matriculation Certificate or Birth Certificate, as applicable) Valid Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) driving licence and 2-year car-driving experience certificate - for Driver applicants Caste certificate (if claiming SC/ST/BC reservation) No Objection Certificate, if currently employed in a Government/Semi-Government Department, Corporation, or Board Discharge book copy, for Ex-servicemen candidates Proof of dependent status, for fee-exempt Ex-servicemen dependents applying for Frash

faq.question: Q1. What is P&H High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: It refers to two recruitment drives by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh: Employment Notice No. 04/DRV/HC/2026 for 25 Driver posts, and Employment Notice No. 05/Frash/HC/2026 for 31 Frash posts.

faq.question: Q2. How many total vacancies are available?
faq.answer: A combined 56 vacancies are available: 25 for Driver (21 General, 3 SC/ST/BC, 1 Ex-Servicemen) and 31 for Frash (26 General, 3 SC/ST/BC, 2 Ex-Servicemen).

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for P&H High Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date for online registration for both the Driver and Frash posts is 18 September 2026, up to 11:59 P.M.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification required?
faq.answer: For Driver, candidates need 10+2 pass with Punjabi/Hindi in matriculation and a valid LMV driving licence. For Frash, the notification requires knowledge of Hindi and the regional language.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for both posts?
faq.answer: Candidates for both Driver and Frash must be between 18 and 35 years of age as on 18/09/2026, with age relaxation for Ex-servicemen equal to their defence service plus 3 years.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee?
faq.answer: Driver: ₹1000/- (General/SC-ST-BC outside Punjab, Haryana, U.T. Chandigarh) or ₹800/- (SC/ST/BC domiciled in these areas, and Ex-servicemen). Frash: ₹700/- or ₹600/- respectively, with a fee exemption for dependents of disabled/deceased Ex-servicemen.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply online?
faq.answer: Candidates can apply only through www.highcourtchd.gov.in, selecting the relevant notice (Driver or Frash), between 28 August 2026 and 18 September 2026.
